content:
Hundreds of flights in the northeastern United States were cancelled due to a technical issue at a major regional air traffic control centre, with all major New York City airports grounding flights for several hours on Monday, coinciding with the arrival of several foreign leaders in the United States for the UN General Assembly.

However, President Trump's flight from Washington to New York departed as scheduled.

The technical fault occurred at a Federal Aviation Administration facility in Philadelphia, the same as the situation in spring 2025 that caused multiple flight disruptions at Newark Liberty International Airport.

Regional control centres typically have two data transmission lines: a primary line and a backup line. The Federal Aviation Administration said a circuit on the primary line failed on Monday morning, and when the system attempted to switch to the backup line, staff discovered that the fibre-optic line had been cut. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed an Amtrak construction crew for the damage.

The fault affected flights at Philadelphia, Kennedy, LaGuardia and Newark airports.

By early afternoon, some flights at LaGuardia, Kennedy and Philadelphia had gradually resumed, but significant delays were still expected for the remainder of the day.

Some airlines allowed passengers to change flights free of charge. The Federal Aviation Administration advised travellers to check flight status with their airlines before heading to the airport.

Federal Aviation Administration administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters that the agency was working to restore the primary line connection as quickly as possible, installing a new circuit on the primary line while simultaneously repairing the backup fibre-optic line. He said it was not yet possible to determine how long this would take. Verizon said its technicians were working to restore service as quickly as possible.

Bedford said: "Repairing the broken fibre-optic cable could take 13 hours; it's a substantial engineering job." The remarks came from a video posted online by a CBS transportation reporter. He also said the Federal Aviation Administration may be able to install the new circuit to restore the primary line before the fibre-optic repair is completed.

The faulty main circuit was part of the national air traffic control system upgrade that was scheduled to be replaced.

Also on Monday, the Federal Aviation Administration began testing a new computer system that uses artificial intelligence to help predict flight allocation conflicts and weather issues, to assist air traffic controllers in replanning routes. However, the system was initially only being tested in the Washington DC area, and therefore appeared unrelated to this grounding incident.
